name: Prefixal Final-r Loss
description: Two prefixes, ir- 'preverb' (PREV) and acir- 'first person inclusive dual agent' (1D.IN.A) lose their final r when they contract with uur- (PREV), ut- (PREV/BEN), or uks- (AOR/JUSS). When r is lost from ir- and acir-, the resulting final i dominates contractions with initial u of the three morphemes.
examples: [{"underlying": "ta- + t- + ir- + ut- + urikatakus", "surface": "tatiiturikataku", "gloss": "I am carrying it under my arm"}]

name: ut- Affrication
description: Final t of the prefix ut- 'preverb (PREV); dative/benefactive (DAT/BEN)' affricates to c when followed by i- 'sequential (SEQ)'. In Skiri, i- SEQ does not dominate over following u in -uks (AOR), unlike in South Band.
examples: [{"underlying": "kuus- + i- + t- + ut- + aar", "surface": "kuustuciʔa", "gloss": "I will do it"}, {"underlying": "i- + s- + ut- + i- + uks- + aar", "surface": "sucuksa", "gloss": "do it! (CONT)"}]

name: Prefixal r-Laryngealization
formal: r -> h / _ r (in tiir-, ar- prefixes)
description: The final r of two evidential prefixes — tiir- 'inferential (INFR)' and ar- 'evidential proper (EV)' — changes to h when preceding an r-initial morpheme. Must be applied before Rule 20 (Degemination) and Rule 15 (Sonorant Reduction).
examples: [{"underlying": "ar- + ri- + at", "surface": "ahiʔat", "gloss": "he went (EV)"}, {"underlying": "tiir- + ra- + kuutik", "surface": "tiihakuutit", "gloss": "he must have killed it"}]

name: t-Laryngealization
description: The stop t becomes laryngeal h when it precedes r. This is a general rule applying across all morpheme boundaries.
examples: [{"underlying": "ta- + t- + raʔuk + -:hus", "surface": "tahuukuʔ", "gloss": "I am making it"}, {"underlying": "pahaat + raʔuk", "surface": "pahaahaʔuk", "gloss": "to redden (CAUS)"}]

name: Metathesis Rule
description: When underlying r is followed by h, the two sounds metathesize. The sequence hr never occurs in surface forms in Skiri (unlike South Band) because hr always reduces to h via Rule 15.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + uur- + hiir", "surface": "tuuhii", "gloss": "he is good (after Rules 14+15 apply)"}]

name: Sonorant r-Reduction
description: This rule reduces the cluster hr to h. Since rh -> hr (Rule 14) always precedes this, the net effect of r+h is h. Must be applied after Rule 14 (Metathesis).
examples: [{"underlying": "ta- + t- + rahuukat", "surface": "tahahuukat", "gloss": "I took it inside"}]

name: h-Loss
formal: h -> NULL / C _ ; h -> NULL / _ C#, CC
description: Laryngeal h is lost: (a) when preceded by a consonant; (b) when it precedes a single word-final consonant or a two-consonant cluster. Two separate environments for deletion.
examples: [{"underlying": "ahiht + -NULL", "surface": "ahiht", "gloss": "be fat (h retained before single C in cluster)"}, {"underlying": "ti- + awahc- + wiitik", "surface": "tiiwacpiitit", "gloss": "he finally sat down"}]

name: Sibilant Hardening
description: The sibilant s becomes the affricate c when it occurs immediately after any consonant.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + ir- + sa + -waa", "surface": "tihcawaa", "gloss": "they are lying (there)"}, {"underlying": "ti- + uur- + sakuriwihc + -:hus", "surface": "tuhcakuriwihcuʔ", "gloss": "the sun is coming out"}]

name: Sibilant Loss
description: When c immediately follows the two-consonant cluster ks, the s is dropped. The environment is specifically after k and before c.
examples: [{"underlying": "i- + s- + ut- + i- + uks- + ciir", "surface": "sucukcii", "gloss": "be energetic!"}]

name: Alveolar Dissimilation
formal: t + t -> ct ; (also t + c -> ct by metathesis)
description: A common underlying sequence t+t across morpheme boundaries: the preceding t changes to c, yielding ct. The less common t+c sequence also metathesizes to ct.
examples: [{"underlying": "ta- + t- + taʔuut", "surface": "tactaʔuut", "gloss": "I stole it"}, {"underlying": "ta- + t- + cak", "surface": "tactat", "gloss": "I shot it (t+c -> ct)"}]

name: Dominant i
description: Seven morpheme combinations where final i/ii of preceding morpheme and initial u of following morpheme contract to i/ii. Applies to: rii- + -uks- -> riiks-; ti-/ii-/ri- + u...]STEM -> tii-/ii-/rii-; -i-/-ir-/acir- + -uur- -> -iir-/-iir-/-aciir-.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + uhurah", "surface": "tiihura", "gloss": "he is alone"}, {"underlying": "ta- + aciir- + uur- + hiir", "surface": "taciihii", "gloss": "you and I are good"}]

name: Consonant Degemination
description: When two identical consonants come together (after prior rules), one is lost. This rule only operates for identical sequences of r and k.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + raar- + raahur", "surface": "tiraraahuʔ", "gloss": "they are ruined (rr -> r)"}, {"underlying": "ti- + uur- + rariir", "surface": "tuurariiʔi", "gloss": "it is a mark (rr -> r, after r-loss at word end)"}]

name: r-Stopping
description: The sonorant r becomes the voiceless stop t when it occurs after an obstruent. Note: t is excluded from triggering obstruents because t+r -> h+r by Rule 13 first.
examples: [{"underlying": "kirik- + raar- + kaa", "surface": "kiriktaahkaa", "gloss": "wear eyeglasses"}, {"underlying": "i- + s- + uks- + riisaapuh", "surface": "sukstiisaapu", "gloss": "stake it!"}]

name: Labial Glide Loss
description: In verb derivation, a w in a preceding syllable is generally lost when the following morpheme begins in w.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + a- + awiwiiʔa", "surface": "taaʔiwiiʔaʔ", "gloss": "he bent over"}, {"underlying": "ta- + t- + katawiwarik k", "surface": "tatkataʔiwarit", "gloss": "I swallowed it"}]

name: Final r Loss
description: Word-final r is always dropped in Skiri.
examples: [{"underlying": "wii- + ta- + t- + ut- + aar", "surface": "wiitatuutaa", "gloss": "I have done it"}]

name: Variants of c
description: The phoneme c has two phonetic variants: [ts] before consonants and word-finally; [ch] (IPA [tsh] or [ch]) before vowels. This is an allophonic rule (surface realization only).
examples: [{"underlying": "capaat", "surface_phonetic": "[chepaat]", "gloss": "woman (c before vowel = ch)"}, {"underlying": "askuc", "surface_phonetic": "[eskuts]", "gloss": "prairie dog (c word-final = ts)"}]

name: Dominant a
description: Modal prefixes ti- (IND), ri- (CONT), kuus...i- (POT.1), ii- (SUBJ) contract with a-dominant morphemes: a- (2.P), a- (PREV; 3.POSS.A), aca- (1D.IN.P), ar- (EV). The i+a -> a.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + a- + piru", "surface": "tapiruʔ", "gloss": "he whipped you"}, {"underlying": "kuus- + a- + i- + kiraawaahc", "surface": "kusaakiraawaʔ", "gloss": "you will forget"}, {"underlying": "ti- + ar- + ut- + asitik", "surface": "wiitaruutasitit", "gloss": "it would happen"}]

name: -his Perfective Reduction
description: The suffix -his 'perfective' (PERF) reduces to s after verb stems ending in a final k. The vowel before k and the hi- of -his are lost, yielding -ks.
examples: [{"underlying": "hak + -his", "surface": "haks", "gloss": "pass by (PERF)"}, {"underlying": "ti- + hak + -his + -ta", "surface": "tihaksta", "gloss": "he is going to pass by"}]

name: Stem-final Vocalic Reduplication
description: Applies to a class of descriptive verbs (approx. half of all VD) in their non-subordinate forms. The stem-final vowel (short or long) reduplicates with a glottal stop inserted.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + pahaat", "surface": "tipahaaʔat", "gloss": "it is red"}, {"underlying": "ti- + huraar- + tararit", "surface": "tihuraahtarariʔit", "gloss": "the ground is burned off"}]

name: Same-vowel Contraction
description: Two identical contiguous vowels contract to a long vowel. The first may be short or long; result is always long. Condition: followed by one or two consonants (not word-final, not before another vowel).
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + uur- + iciisat", "surface": "tuuriciisat", "gloss": "he is tired"}, {"underlying": "ku- + ii- + ut- + kaksaa", "surface": "kuʔuutkaksaa", "gloss": "if he could holler for him"}]

name: u-Domination
formal: V/VV + u OR u(u) + V -> uu / _ C(C)V
description: In a sequence of two vowels where any vowel in the sequence is u, the vowels contract to long uu. The first vowel may be long or short. Condition: before one or two consonants.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + uur- + iciisat", "surface": "tuuriciisat", "gloss": "he is tired"}]

name: Contraction of i and a
formal: i(i) + a(a) OR a(a) + i -> ii / _ C(C)V
description: Combinations of i or ii followed by a or aa, or a/aa followed by i, contract to ii. (In South Band Pawnee and Arikara the result is ee.)
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + atkaʔu", "surface": "tiitkuʔ", "gloss": "he hears"}]

name: Assibilation of raar-
description: The final consonant of raar- 'plural; iterative' assibilates when followed by a stem-initial t. The r+t sequence becomes c.
examples: [{"underlying": "ti- + raar- + takasis", "surface": "tiracakasis", "gloss": "they are close together"}]

name: Final-s Loss
description: Certain nouns and suffixes ending in s regularly lose it word-finally but retain it when another morpheme follows. E.g. kuhkus 'swine' -> kuhku in isolation but kuhkuskaʔit 'salt pork' in compounds. The aspectual suffix -:hus/-hus (IMPF) also loses final s word-finally.
examples: [{"underlying": "kuhkus", "surface": "kuhku", "gloss": "swine (independent)"}, {"underlying": "ti- + kiikaa + -:hus", "surface": "tikiikaahuʔ", "gloss": "he is drinking (IMPF, word-final s lost)"}]
